All K are S.

No S is a B.

__
 
• Article 108 of the Constitution of India provides for joint sitting of both the Houses.
 
• It must be noted here that the provision of joint sitting is applicable to ordinary bills or financial bills only and not to money bills or Constitutional amendment bills.
 
• The joint sitting of the Parliament is called by the President and is presided over by the Speaker or, in his absence, by the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha or in his absence, the Deputy-Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

• Procedure: The procedures of joint sessions are subject to modifications and variations as the Speaker may consider necessary or appropriate.

questions.question: In an ecosystem, vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called ______.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of identification and enumeration of plant and animal species of an ecosystem gives its species composition.
 
• The vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called >stratification.
 
• For example, trees occupy the top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Species composition**

 
 
• It differs from one ecosystem to another depending upon geography, topography, and climate.
 
• Each ecosystem has a biotic community composed of a particular grouping of species.
 
• Maximum species composition occurs in tropical rainforests and coral reefs.
 
• The minimum occurs in deserts and arctic regions.
 
 
 
• **Stratifications**
 
 
• Stratification is the occurrence of vertical zonation in the ecosystem & indicates the presence of favorable environmental conditions, for e.g., trees occupy top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs, and herbs & grasses occupy the bottom layers. >Stratification helps in the accommodation of a large number & types of plants in the same area.
 
• It also provides a number of microhabitat & niches for various types of animals.
 
• It is absent or poor where environmental conditions are unfavorable, e.g. desert ecosystems have very few trees & shrubs.
 
 
 
• **Standing crop**
 
 
• A standing crop is an amount of living biomass in an ecosystem. It indicates the productivity & luxuriance of growth.
 
• It is expressed in the form of the number or biomass of organisms per unit area.
 
• A terrestrial ecosystem with a high standing crop possesses a forest while the one with a low standing crop occurs in grassland followed by the arid ecosystem.

• Revenues received by the government by way of **direct taxes and indirect taxes**, money borrowed and receipts from loans and expenses made by it, excluding the exceptional items, are part of the Consolidated Fund.
 
• This fund was constituted under **Article 266 (1)** of the Constitution of India.
 
• All government expenditure is made from this fund, except exceptional items which are met from the Contingency Fund or the Public Account.
 
• No money can be withdrawn from this fund without the Parliament’s approval. 
 
•

• the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of State and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.
 
• debt charges for which the Government of India is liable including interest, sinking fund charges and redemption charges, and other expenditures related to the raising of loans and the service and redemption of Debt.
 
• the salaries, allowances, and pensions were payable to or in respect of Judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• the pension payable to or in respect of Judges of the federal court the pension payable to on respect of the Judges of the High Court.
 
• the salary allowances and pension payable to or in respect of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

questions.question: The claim for ‘swarajya’ or self-government within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in 1906 by:

__
 
• The claim for **"swarajya" or self-government** within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in the **Calcutta session of 1906.**
 
• The session was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, who is considered the **"Grand Old Man of India" **for his contributions to the Indian independence movement. 
 
• In his presidential address, Naoroji called for **"self-government or swaraj like the United Kingdom or the colonies"** of Australia or Canada. 
 
• This was a significant shift in the Congress's position, as it had previously been more focused on seeking limited reforms within the British Raj.
 
• The Calcutta session's resolution on swaraj was a compromise between the **"moderates" and "extremists"** within the Congress. 
 
• The **moderates, led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, wanted to pursue a gradual path to self-government, while the extremists, led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, wanted to demand complete independence. 
 
• The resolution on swaraj represented a middle ground, calling for self-government within the British Empire, but with a degree of autonomy that would be similar to that of self-governing colonies.

questions.question: If a, b, c are all non-zero and a + b + c = 0, find the value of (a²)/(bc)+(b²)/(ca)+(c²)/(ab).

Let a = 1, b = 1, and c = −2 so that the condition a + b + c = 0 is satisfied.

Substitute these values directly into the expression: a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab)

a, b, c are non-zero real numbers.

a + b + c = 0

⇒ Take the LCM of the denominators bc, ca, and ab, which is abc.

⇒ Expression = (a × a² + b × b² + c × c²) / abc

⇒ Expression = (a³ + b³ + c³) / abc

⇒ Substitute a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc (from the formula above)

⇒ Expression = 3abc / abc

⇒ Expression = 3

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, the first factor on the right side of the standard identity becomes zero. This eliminates the entire right-hand side, leaving a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Value Putting Strategy

For cyclic and homogeneous expressions dependent on a condition like a + b + c = 0, substituting simple non-zero integers (like 1, 1, and −2) gives the result instantly without requiring complex algebraic manipulations.

questions.question: The speeds of two bodies are in the ratio 2 : 3. If the difference in the time taken to cover 50 m is 10 sec, then find the difference in their speeds.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of speeds = 2 : 3 → **Ratio** of time taken = 3 : 2 (since distance is constant).

Difference in time units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = 10 sec ∴ Time taken by first body = 3 × 10 = 30 sec; Time taken by second body = 2 × 10 = 20 sec.

Speed₁ = 50/30 = 5/3 m/sec and Speed₂ = 50/20 = 5/2 m/sec.

Difference in speeds = 5/2 − 5/3 = (15 − 10) / 6 = 5/6 m/sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/6 m/sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **speeds** = 2 : 3

**Distance** = 50 m

**Time Difference** = 10 sec

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9396876e9ab256e167679012be849f62617479753ecae6f83af98710df97608b.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speeds of the two bodies be 2x m/sec and 3x m/sec.

⇒ Time taken by first body (T₁) = 50 / 2x = 25/x sec

⇒ Time taken by second body (T₂) = 50 / 3x sec

According to the question, the difference in time is 10 sec:

⇒ T₁ − T₂ = 10

⇒ (25/x) − (50/3x) = 10

⇒ (75 − 50) / 3x = 10

⇒ 25 / 3x = 10

⇒ 30x = 25

⇒ x = 25 / 30 = 5/6

The difference in their speeds is (3x − 2x) = x.

⇒ Difference = 5/6 m/sec.

Comparing this result with the given options, we find it matches Option (2).

**∴ The correct answer is 5/6 m/sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Law

When the distance traveled is **constant**, the speed is **inversely proportional** to the time taken (Speed ∝ 1/Time). If the ratio of speeds is a:b, then the ratio of time taken is b:a.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr to m/sec**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/sec to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (s₂ − s₁). If they move in opposite directions, it is the **sum** (s₁ + s₂).</p

• **Unreflective **- as it is the most direct and e**xact opposite of being in a state of deep or serious thought, which "pensive" implies. "Frivolous" could be considered an antonym as well, but it also carries implications of a lack of seriousness or value, which is not inherently present in the definition of "pensive".** Therefore, "Unreflective" would be the most appropriate antonym among the given options.
